To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the demand for healthy foods is higher for individuals who are better educated, who participate in a health training, who are active in sports, who have higher incomes, and who are older.

(i) the demand for a diverse diet is positively influenced by age, education, health-related knowledge, health behaviour, and health training; (ii) a diverse diet is negatively influenced by income, gender and the presence of children in the household; and (iii) the demand for healthy foods is positively influenced by education, health training, sport activity and health knowledge, and negatively by age, income, and gender.
The demand for healthy food is influenced by age, knowledge, attitudinally and behaviourally variables and the health value of a food basket, but not by income and price.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an important aspect of healthy eating and provides a new and useful indicator for healthy food diversity.
the development of an innovative healthy eating indicator and its application in an economic approach.
the demand for healthy diversity and the factors influencing this demand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the demand for healthy diversity in food consumption is influenced by socio-economic and demographic characteristics and health-related factors.
healthy eating is not just about eating healthy food, but also about eating a variety of healthy food.
healthy food diversity is an indicator for healthy eating and should be considered as a new target for public health nutrition policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the demand for healthy and diverse eating is positively influenced by education level, sport activity, participation in a training course and by the knowledge of health effects of food diversity.

the demand for diversity of a healthy diet is not only influenced by the individual's knowledge and attitude towards healthy eating, but also by his or her behaviour and health-related characteristics.
a higher diversity of a food consumption pattern is associated with higher health benefits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a healthy diet is a complex phenomenon, and it is important that the demand for healthy diversity is considered in future studies.
the demand for healthy foods and healthy eating is positively affected by education and health-related behaviour.
health promotion and nutrition policy should not focus on the healthiness of the food basket only but should also consider the diversity of the diet.
